title: Asian Games 2026: India Joint 10th After Day 1 as China, Japan Lead
excerpt: India opened its Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games medal account with two shooting silvers from Elavenil Valarivan, while China and hosts Japan set the early pace with 20 medals each.
body:
• India ended the first day of medal competition at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games with two silver medals, both in women's 10m air rifle shooting, placing the country joint 10th in the standings.
  • China leads the table with 11 gold, 6 silver and 3 bronze (20 medals), followed by hosts Japan with 6 gold, 7 silver and 7 bronze (20 medals).
  • Elavenil Valarivan won both of India's medals — team silver with Sonam Uttam Maskar and Vidarsa Vinod, then individual silver, finishing 0.6 points behind Japan's Hinata Taichi.
  • Beyond the medals, India assured at least a bronze in women's traditional MMA, stormed into the women's cricket final, and opened hockey with 19-0 and 13-1 wins.

Where India stands after Day 1

India's medal campaign at the 20th Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya is underway, and the opening day of medal competition ended with the country joint 10th in the standings on two silver medals — both from the shooting range. Elavenil Valarivan was the central figure in each: she combined with Sonam Uttam Maskar and Games debutant Vidarsa Vinod to take team silver in the women's 10m air rifle, then added an individual silver later in the day.

The individual final was decided by the finest of margins. Valarivan, 27, shot 252.4 to finish 0.6 points behind Japan's Hinata Taichi, whose 253.0 set an Asian Games record. South Korea's Ban Hyojin took bronze with 230.4. Valarivan led for much of the final before three loose shots in the closing stages let Taichi through — a near-miss that nonetheless ended her wait for an Asian Games podium after two previous appearances without one.

The full Day 1 medal table

China wasted no time asserting its usual dominance, collecting 11 gold, 6 silver and 3 bronze for a 20-medal haul. Hosts Japan matched that total with 6 gold, 7 silver and 7 bronze. South Korea sits third with 4 gold, 3 silver and 7 bronze (14 medals), while Kazakhstan (3 gold, 2 bronze) and Thailand (3 gold) round out the top five.

Beyond the medals: India's Day 1 in full

The shooting silvers were the headline, but the day's foundations may matter more. Suchika Tariyal assured India at least a bronze in the women's traditional MMA 60kg event by reaching the semifinals — a guaranteed podium that upgrades in color if she wins her next bout. The women's cricket team stormed into the final after beating Bangladesh, powered by Shafali Verma's maiden T20I century. Both hockey teams opened emphatically: the women beat Uzbekistan 19-0 and the men beat Indonesia 13-1. India's badminton and women's table tennis teams also began with victories, keeping multiple team-event medal paths alive.

The shooting haul carries extra weight given history — the discipline produced a record 22 medals for India at the Hangzhou Asian Games, and an early double-silver suggests the ranges in Aichi could be productive again.

The diaspora view

For Indian fans watching from the United States and elsewhere abroad, the medal table is the daily scoreboard that matters most — and Day 1's joint-10th place is a starting point, not a verdict. India's 107-medal haul at Hangzhou was built slowly across the fortnight, and the sports where India traditionally surges — athletics, wrestling, boxing, kabaddi — have barely begun.

What to watch on Day 2

September 21 brings new fronts: kabaddi begins and boxing gets underway, per the Games schedule. Tariyal's MMA semifinal is the most immediate medal watch — she is already assured of bronze and fights for a place in the final. More shooting medal events are on the calendar, and the badminton and table tennis team campaigns continue. Looking slightly further ahead, the women's cricket team plays its gold-medal match on Tuesday, and the men's hockey team faces Sri Lanka the same day. If Day 1 was about opening the account, Day 2 is where the tally starts to move.
